rule: Interactive touch targets must be at least 44x44px (iOS) / 48x48dp (Android/Material), including padding — not just the visible glyph.
Body text must meet WCAG AA contrast (4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large text ≥18px/14px-bold) against its background in every stated color mode.
No icon-only interactive control without an accessible label (visible text, aria-label, or tooltip-on-focus) — an icon alone is not self-explanatory to all users.
Any non-trivial motion (standard or complex tier) must have a reduced-motion fallback (instant or near-instant transition) honoring prefers-reduced-motion.
Status/meaning must never be conveyed by color alone — pair with icon, text label, or pattern for colorblind and low-vision users.
Every interactive element must have a visible keyboard focus state distinct from hover state — never remove focus outlines without a replacement.
Any action taking longer than ~300ms must show a loading/pending state — never leave the UI silently unresponsive.
Every error state must state what went wrong in plain language and offer a concrete next action (retry, contact support, go back) — never a bare error code alone.
Destructive or irreversible actions (delete, cancel subscription, overwrite) require an explicit confirmation step naming what will be lost.
No unintended horizontal scroll on the page body at any target viewport width down to 375px — only deliberately scrollable regions (tables, carousels) may scroll horizontally.
Every form input has a visible, associated label — placeholder text alone never substitutes for a label.
Every list/collection view defines an explicit empty state with guidance on what to do next — never a blank screen when there's no data yet.
